title: Ember AI - POC scoping (open models)
next_steps: Redwood to share open-model shortlist + perf profiles by 2026-03-13
Customer to send sample prompt set and 2 weeks of anonymized logs by 2026-03-15
Schedule pilot kickoff + infra runbook review w/ Tom for 2026-03-18
action_items: Marcus - run small perf benchmark (latency/cost) on 3 candidate models by 2026-03-13
Ravi - provide 2 weeks of request traces and target p99 latency by 2026-03-15
Lena - send pricing/estimate for 3-month dedicated pilot by 2026-03-14
summary: POC scoping focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for Ember AI's multilingual customer support summarization workload. Key criteria: accuracy on domain docs, multilingual support (en, es, pt), p99 latency < 500ms for 128-token responses, cost target ~ $0.006/token effective via batching/caching. Timeline: pilot kickoff mid-March, 3-week benchmark phase, decision by early April.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to scope the POC with Ember AI. quick intro round?
[00:08] Sofia Alvarez: Hi, Sofia here, CTO at Ember. we own the core product and the summarization model.
[00:13] Ravi Patel: Ravi, lead ml, i'll be doing the evals and integration.
[00:16] Marcus Chen: Marcus from Redwood, solutions engineer. i'll handle benchmarking and perf.
[00:20] Marta Sousa: Marta, product — i'll help with acceptance criteria.
[00:23] Tom Nguyen: Tom, infra — mainly VPC and networking.
[00:27] Lena Park: Great. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, open-model shortlist, tradeoffs, and next steps.
[00:34] Sofia: Sounds good. high level — we run customer support summarization across english, spanish, and portuguese. volumes: about 25k requests/day now, peaks to 40k on weekdays. average response length target ~ 70-150 tokens.
[00:46] Ravi: Important — we have proprietary domain docs (legal/terms) so output quality on domain is priority. Also latency: we'd like p95 < 300ms and p99 < 500ms for the majority of flows. cost is also a factor as we scale.
[01:02] Marcus: okay noted. For POC we usually pick 2-3 open models that balance quality/cost. Based on your multilingual requirement and domain, initial shortlist could be Mistral-small follow by Llama2-13B q4 if licensing allows, and a quantized MPT-X variant.
[01:20] Ravi: Mistral-small? i'm not familiar — is that the one that does well cross-lingual?
[01:24] Lena Park: quick note — some names may be mis-read in the transcript: Mistral / Mistral 7B/ small, Llama2 13B — but yeah. Mistral and Llama variants have different tradeoffs. Mistral tends to be lighter and cheaper, Llama2-13B usually higher quality for domain finetune.
[01:40] Marta: do we have examples of where quality differs for PT and ES?
[01:44] Marcus Chen: we can run our multi-ling evals. Historically Llama2-13B without instruction fine-tune can struggle slightly on PT, but with prompt engineering and a small supervised fine-tune it's fine. Mistral variants can be surprisingly good but sometimes hallucinate on niche legal terms.
[02:00] Sofia: Hallucination is a hard blocker for us. We need factuality checks and the ability to tune quickly.
[02:05] Marcus: understood. for the POC success criteria propose: 1) ROUGE/ROUGE-L and BLEU-ish style quality target vs your golden set with > 0.78 normalized F1, 2) p99 latency < 500ms for 128-token avg response at target concurrency, 3) cost per 1k requests below our internal threshold ~ $6-$8 after batching/caching, 4) low hallucination rate (< 1% critical hallucinations on sampled tests).
[02:32] Ravi: the 0.78 threshold — that sounds reasonable as a starting point. we'll provide a golden set of ~500 labeled examples across EN/ES/PT.
[02:41] Tom Nguyen: on infra — we plan to run pilot in our AWS account inside a VPC. need to confirm network egress and KMS integration. how does Redwood handle private deploys?
[02:51] Lena Park: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. for POC we typically run in hosted mode or a dedicated private sandbox. Marcus, can you cover networking options?
[02:59] Marcus Chen: yes — we can deploy a dedicated pool in our hosted infra with VPC peering or you can run Redwood Private (control plane with your VPC). For initial bench we suggest dedicated hosted pool with a private subnet to reduce friction. KMS for key wrapping yes supported, we'll share the runbook.
[03:18] Marta: timeline wise — what's realistic?
[03:20] Lena Park: propose: this week send prompt set + logs, by next Friday (2026-03-13) Redwood runs perf + quality benchmarks on 3 candidates, week after we review results and pick 1 model to run a longer pilot (2-3 weeks) with your infra. decision by early April.
[03:35] Sofia: that timeline works.
[03:36] Ravi: quick Q on billing: we were exploring dedicated vs hosted — for an initial POC which is cheaper?
[03:41] Marcus Chen: hosted dedicated pool (reserved small pool) tends to be cheaper per-token for steady throughput but has setup time. For short POC hosted shared endpoints with caching and aggressive batching may be fastest to stand up. We'll provide estimates.
[03:56] Marta: what about safety and audit logs? we need audit trails for content transformations.
[03:59] Lena Park: Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and audit logs with retention options. We also have role-based access and SSO/SAML. We'll attach SOC2 docs.
[04:11] Tom Nguyen: also need to ensure data retention controls and ability to disable long-term storage for PII.
[04:16] Marcus Chen: yes we can toggle retention per-tenant, and we have integrations with customer KMS so data at rest encryption meets your requirements.
[04:25] Sofia: back to models — can you list concrete candidate models for the benchmark?
[04:28] Marcus Chen: sure. Candidate A: Mistral-7B-instruct (fast, lower cost, good zero-shot), Candidate B: Llama-2-13B-instruct (higher quality, larger footprint, needs more memory), Candidate C: MPT-30B-FT-quant (domain friendly after fine-tune, heavier but good for legal phrasing), Candidate D (optional): GEMINI-like closed model via partner if needed but that's out of scope for open-model POC.
[04:54] Ravi: would you quantize Llama2-13B? memory footprint will matter.
[04:58] Marcus Chen: yes we can run int8/4 quant variants — on our runtime quantization reduces memory and often keeps quality within 1-3% depending on metric. We'll include q4 variants in the perf run.
[05:10] Marta: what benchmarks will you run? latency at different concurrencies, cost estimate, quality vs golden set, and hallucination checks?
[05:16] Marcus Chen: exactly. We'll run end-to-end latency (p50/95/99) for payload sizes 64/128/256 tokens, throughput tests at target concurrency (simulate 100, 300, 600 rps), and quality evals on the 500 labeled examples across languages. Also measure memory usage and estimate cost per 1k requests with batching/caching enabled.
[05:35] Ravi: on the simulation — our traffic is bursty; can you simulate daily peaks?
[05:38] Marcus Chen: yes we'll do peak burst tests. Also show impact of prefix caching for repeated user context.
[05:45] Lena Park: action items recap: Marcus runs perf + quality by 2026-03-13, Ravi shares logs + golden set by 2026-03-15, Lena sends pricing and SOC2 docs by 2026-03-14. Pilot kickoff 2026-03-18 pending infra checks.
[06:00] Sofia: perfect. small question — any quick guidance on prompt templates for multilingual summarization?
[06:05] Marcus Chen: keep prompts language-labeled (e.g., [ES] Summarize: ) and keep instructions concise. We'll share examples. For domain: give a short instruction and few-shot examples in target language to reduce hallucination.
[06:18] Ravi: last thing — can Redwood run token-level cost breakdown per model?
[06:21] Lena Park: yes, Redwood Console will provide per-route token breakdown and model-level cost estimates. We'll include that in the results.
[06:29] Marta: thanks all — we'll follow up in email.
[06:33] Lena Park: thanks everyone, we'll send the shortlist and runbook.
[06:36] [call ends]
